newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dlr vols stuck as spot ranges solidify.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr vols stuck as spot ranges solidify.

text.p: Dollar options were a touch easier in early trading as spot dollar/mark and dollar/yen hovered in the thin ranges near multi-year highs.

Traders said soft first-quarter U.S. employment cost data Tuesday has cast enough doubt over a U.S. interest rate rise next month to cap dollar/mark about 1.74 until Friday's key April employment report. The 1.72 area is firm support, with option risk reversals still showing slight bias to dollar calls.
Dollar/yen trading is dominated, meantime, by talk of a large options position expiring this week with a reverse knockout about the recent high at 127.20.

"The expiry of this option is prompting some considerable spot resistance to the upside and it's hard to see any fresh breakout before Friday," said one trader at a U.S. investment house. "The payrolls is again becoming the focus and Friday expiries in particular are well bid as a result."
One month dollar/mark and dollar/yen vols were trading in lock-step at 8.40/8.70 percent, with dollar/mark a touch softer from Tuesday and dollar/yen a touch higher.
One-month 25 delta risk reversals in dollar/yen were unchanged at 0.1 percentage point around par showing a neutral bias at current levels.
One-month dollar/mark risk reversals still show a slight bias to dollar calls at 0.0/0.3 point but this is down slightly from 0.1/0.4 point yesterday.
Dollar/mark and sterling/dollar vols on options expiring Friday are more than point higher than one-week vols due to the payrolls report and the UK election, traders said.

Sterling vols on options of a month or longer, however, still show little movement. One-month sterling/mark was unchanged at 9.30/60 percent and risk reversals around par while one-month cable was up a touch at 7.40/7.70 pct vs 7.10/7.40 pct late Tuesday. --Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6762
